title: Inbox Zero Is the Wrong Goal
summary: Chasing an empty inbox optimizes the wrong metric. Here is what an intelligent inbox optimizes instead.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


An empty inbox measures activity, not outcomes: you can hit zero by archiving everything and still miss the three threads that mattered. The better target is making sure the email that needs you reaches you first and nothing important drops. That is what an intelligent inbox optimizes, and it is how Slashy's triage and follow-up detection are built.


## Why this matters


Email is where most knowledge work actually happens, yet the tools treat it as a dumb list. An intelligent inbox changes the unit of work from "messages" to "outcomes." That shift compounds the more it learns about how you actually communicate.


## How Slashy approaches it


Slashy was built AI-native from the first commit. The in-house memory system adapts continuously to the email you send, receive, and respond to, so drafting, triage, and scheduling get sharper over weeks rather than stalling at day-one accuracy.


## What to do next


Start a trial and let the memory system watch one week of real inbox activity. The difference between day one and day thirty is the whole point.
